title: Reusable launcher turnaround, TPS, maintenance economics and crew-abort audit for OTA-TEC-0083
question: Source-grounded audit of the exact OTA-TEC-0083 document. Using primary, peer-reviewed and official launch-system sources, assess: (1) what actually drives turnaround time and marginal/average cost in reusable launch systems; (2) inspection and replacement burdens for thermal-protection systems, engines, tanks and structures under repeated ascent/reentry cycles; (3) whether 24–72 h turnaround is an engineering target, demonstrated capability or still speculative for fully reusable orbital systems; (4) crew-abort architectures for reusable launchers and whether a launch escape tower is truly a generic standard; (5) engine-out/redundancy limits in clustered engines across ascent phases; and (6) which real evidence can support the dossier without implying that reuse alone guarantees its fictional ticket prices. Identify wording that should be narrowed or reclassified. Do NOT evaluate or alter [F] ticket prices, operator names, passenger count, fictional schedules, Mars Credits, unlocks, journeys or other NOXIA balancing values.
why_now: OTA-TEC-0083 is canonical and uses turnaround, reusable TPS and crew-safety assumptions as important technical anchors; these should be audited independently from fictional economics and balancing.
real_world_anchor: Falcon 9 and reusable launch operations, Starship development, thermal protection, engine reuse, crew launch abort systems and launch economics.
novelty_reason: First source-pinned operations, TPS and crew-safety audit of the canonical Starport-Launcher technical object.
